Mitiga investigated an ongoing phishing campaign, active since at least April 2020, that impersonates Microsoft Office 365 voicemail notifications to steal user credentials. The emails are sent from legitimate Office 365 accounts that have been compromised by an unknown threat actor. The campaign has targeted small and medium-sized businesses and major financial institutions in the United States and Australia, particularly C-level executives.

After a victim clicks the voicemail link, the traffic is redirected through several proxies, including AWS load balancers, before reaching a compromised legitimate website and ultimately a fake Office 365 sign-in page. Mitiga identified more than 40 compromised SMB websites used in this infrastructure, while the fake login pages were hosted on Oracle Cloud resources or, in some cases, AWS S3 buckets imitating Zoom invitations. Entered credentials were sent to compromised legitimate websites, potentially enabling deeper access to victim organizations or business email compromise.

Mitiga found parallel versions of the phishing pages with small code and infrastructure differences, which it said may indicate a third-party phishing platform used by several sub-groups. The researchers also found references to Asian locations and Indonesian words in the page code, but cautioned that these could be false flags. Mitiga recommends enforcing Office 365 multi-factor authentication and reviewing mailbox forwarding rules, hidden folders, login and settings changes, and suspicious account activity.

  • Code references to Asian locations and Indonesian words were identified in the phishing pages, but Mitiga cautioned that these could be deliberate false flags rather than reliable attribution evidence.

CIRA, or Cloud Investigation and Response Automation, is presented as a way to help organizations respond to and recover from cloud breaches more effectively.

CIRA can help address gaps in cloud and SaaS incident-response skills, ensure the collection and analysis of investigation data, and test whether response practices work in cloud environments before an incident occurs. The article also highlights that SaaS applications are often independently adopted and managed by business units, which can reduce central IT visibility and make policy enforcement harder. CIRA does not replace cloud security controls or policies, but it can provide greater visibility and help organizations prepare to respond and recover when SaaS-related risks materialize.

  • An organization can have skilled personnel and an incident-response vendor yet still be unprepared if it is not continuously collecting the cloud data required for a complete investigation.
  • Cloud incident-response methods should be tested before an incident because practices and testing frequency that work for on-premises systems may not work the same way for cloud and SaaS services.
  • Decentralized SaaS adoption creates a governance problem: business units may independently deploy services, limiting central IT visibility and making it difficult to verify that security policies are actually being followed.

The article argues that companies using cloud services and online business software need better ways to investigate and recover from security break-ins. Many security teams are experienced with systems they run themselves but may lack the skills, information, and tested plans needed for cloud and software-as-a-service incidents. This affects large organizations whose departments independently use tools such as HR, customer-management, marketing, and collaboration services, making it harder to see what is happening and ensure company rules are followed. The stakes are high because a weak response after a cloud break-in can leave an organization unable to quickly understand, contain, and recover from the damage.

OPEN SOURCE ↗

This is a general best-practice perspective on improving cloud and SaaS incident response with CIRA, not coverage of a specific incident, vulnerability, or urgent finding. It may be useful for security leaders evaluating cloud-response readiness, but it offers limited concrete technical detail.

Microsoft's Wormable SMBv3 Flaw in a Pandemic Context

The article argues that although Microsoft’s SMBv3 flaw (CVE-2020-0796) was unlikely to cause an immediate cyber pandemic on its own, future worms combining multiple vulnerabilities could spread too quickly for manual response. Organizations should consider automated, aggressive network quarantine measures before such an outbreak occurs.
KEY POINTS
  • 01A new wormable vulnerability in Microsoft’s SMBv3 protocol was reported during the COVID-19 pandemic.
  • 02The article compares computer worms with biological viruses, noting that worms can infect and begin spreading in seconds to minutes while also potentially remaining dormant before activating their payload.
  • 03The article describes shutting down an entire network as the cybersecurity equivalent of a total lockdown, an effective but highly disruptive response to rapidly spreading malware.
  • 04Selective quarantine of suspected compromised systems would need to be fully automated because a computer worm can begin infecting other systems within seconds.
  • 05The article states that the SMBv3 vulnerability alone is not sufficiently contagious to cause a large cyber pandemic, but combining vulnerabilities across different infection paths could create a more dangerous worm.

The article examines a newly reported wormable vulnerability in Microsoft’s SMBv3 protocol during the COVID-19 pandemic. It compares self-spreading computer worms with biological viruses, arguing that both can infect before causing visible damage or activating a harmful payload. The major difference is speed: computer worms can settle in and begin spreading within seconds or minutes, rather than the hours or days associated with Coronavirus.

Using pandemic containment as an analogy, the article describes shutting down an entire network as the digital equivalent of a total lockdown: disruptive, but potentially preferable to widespread compromise. It also presents selective quarantine of suspected infected computers as a less disruptive option, but says it would need to be fully automated because worms spread too quickly for manual decisions. The SMBv3 issue alone is described as insufficiently contagious to cause a major cyber pandemic, though the article warns that several vulnerabilities across different infection paths could be combined into a more dangerous worm.

  • The article argues that computer-worm containment has an advantage over disease containment because systems can detect a compromised computer attempting to spread to others through its network traffic.
  • Because computer worms can begin spreading within seconds, the article concludes that selective isolation cannot depend on human decision-making and must be automated.
  • The article highlights that the central preparedness question is whether organizations will authorize an automated system to shut down or isolate systems based on suspicion alone, before the full scale of an outbreak is known.

The article discusses a newly identified weakness in Microsoft’s file-sharing system that could allow a self-spreading harmful program to move between computers. It says this particular problem is unlikely to cause a worldwide digital outbreak by itself, but several weaknesses used together could spread extremely quickly through organizations’ networks. The main concern is that businesses may need automated systems that can quickly isolate suspected infected computers, even though doing so could temporarily disrupt normal work.

FDA Flags Cyber, AI Risks in Autonomous Medical Robots

FDA and cybersecurity experts warn that autonomous and remotely operated medical robots can expose patients to real-time harm if attackers hijack communications, inject commands, or disrupt device connectivity. They urge cyber-informed clinical risk assessments that link technical threats directly to patient-safety outcomes.
KEY POINTS
  • 01Federal regulators and cybersecurity experts warn that AI-enabled and remotely connected robotic medical devices can create patient-safety risks from cyberattacks, AI malfunctions, and communications failures.
  • 02Phil Englert of Health-ISAC said remote or autonomous medical devices should undergo cyber-informed clinical risk assessments that connect cybersecurity threats to clinical-care and patient-safety outcomes.
  • 03Englert said the communication link between an operator and a remotely operated medical device becomes part of the device’s attack surface.
  • 04Potential actions against these devices include session hijacking, command injection, credential theft, denial-of-service conditions, and introducing packet loss or latency.
  • 05According to Englert, a cyberattack could affect clinical decision-making or alter patient treatment in real time, increasing the potential for patient harm.

Federal regulators and cybersecurity experts are warning that artificial intelligence and remote connectivity in robotic medical devices can introduce risks to patient safety. Cyberattacks, AI malfunctions, and communications failures could cause harm before clinicians have time to intervene. The concern extends beyond stolen patient data or temporary device outages because treatment could be affected during a procedure.

Phil Englert of Health-ISAC said remote or autonomous medical devices should receive cyber-informed clinical risk assessments that connect technical threats to clinical-care and patient-safety outcomes. He noted that the communication link between an operator and a device becomes part of the attack surface. Potential threats include session hijacking, injected commands, credential theft, denial-of-service conditions, packet loss, and latency that interferes with device performance.

  • For remote robotic devices, the connection between the clinician and the device must be treated as part of the system that can be targeted, rather than as a separate operational detail.
  • The article emphasizes evaluating cyber risks by their direct effect on treatment and patient safety, not only by data loss or device downtime.
  • Packet loss and connection delays can be safety-relevant because they may interfere with a device’s performance during a procedure.
  • The potential impact is time-critical: interference could influence clinical decisions or alter treatment before clinicians can intervene.

Federal regulators and security experts are warning that medical robots controlled partly by artificial intelligence or from a distance can create new dangers if their connections fail or are tampered with. During a procedure, someone could interfere with the link between a clinician and the robot, potentially delaying or changing treatment before the clinician can respond. This matters because the impact could be immediate harm to patients, not just stolen health information or a temporarily unavailable device.

OPEN SOURCE ↗

The article provides useful context on safety risks in autonomous and remote medical robots, but it does not report a specific incident, vulnerability, patch, or active threat campaign. It is primarily a broad risk and best-practice perspective.

Automated concept

automated systems concept

automated tool tool

automated workloads concept

Automation concept

autonomous AI concept
Autonomous AI is artificial intelligence that can make decisions or take actions with limited human direction.
Autonomy concept
Autonomy is the degree to which a system can make decisions and act without direct human control.

backups concept

canada

capture concept

Google's official online marketplace for Chrome browser extensions and themes, occasionally plagued by malicious extensions.

cloud resources concept

cluster concept

code change concept

code execution technique

coding concept

command execution technique

commit concept

commits concept

compliance concerns concept

compromise concept

compromised accounts concept

compromised credentials concept

Compromised devices are computers, phones, or systems that attackers have gained unauthorized control over.
compromised endpoints concept
Computers, phones, servers, or other connected devices that an attacker has successfully breached.
Compromised hosts concept
Computers or servers that attackers have successfully taken control of.
compromised legitimate websites technique
Real websites that attackers have broken into and altered to harm or deceive their visitors.

Compromised systems concept

compromised websites concept

computer systems concept

confidential information concept

configuration data concept

Network requests and data flows traveling between users, devices, and online services.

containers concept

crafted requests technique

credential concept

credentials concept

also: cryptocurrency theft, cryptoassets, digital assets, virtual assets
Cryptocurrency Bridges concept
Services or software that move cryptocurrency assets between separate blockchain networks.
also: bridges
Cryptocurrency miners malware
Programs that use computer processing power to help create or validate cryptocurrency transactions, sometimes without the owner's permission.
cryptocurrency thefts concept
Cryptocurrency thefts are crimes where attackers steal digital currencies such as Bitcoin or Ethereum.
cryptocurrency wallet product
A cryptocurrency wallet is software or hardware used to store and use the keys that control digital coins.
cryptocurrency wallet data concept
Information about cryptocurrency wallets, including keys, balances, and transaction history, often targeted by thieves.
Cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases concept
These are secret recovery words that can restore and fully control a cryptocurrency wallet.
Cryptographic key concept
A cryptographic key is a secret value used to lock or unlock encrypted information.
cryptojacking technique
Cryptojacking is when attackers secretly use someone else’s computer power to mine cryptocurrency.
curl
curl is a command-line tool used to transfer data to or from servers using protocols like HTTP and HTTPS.
also: curl -sI --http2 https://<host>/
cursor
Cursor is an AI-assisted code editor built for software developers.
Customer Account concept
A personal account that lets a customer sign in to a company's service and manage their information.
Customer accounts concept
Customer accounts are user records and logins that let customers access a company's services.
Customer and Partner Systems concept
Customer and partner systems are the computer systems operated by an organization's customers, suppliers, or other business associates.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
Customer endpoint concept
A customer endpoint is a user's device or system, such as a laptop or server, that connects to a service or network.
Customer endpoints concept
Customer endpoints are user devices or systems, such as laptops or servers, that belong to or serve customers.
Customer environments concept
Customer environments are the computers, cloud services, networks, and settings used by an organization.
Customer Names concept
Names that identify customers and may be sensitive when exposed in a data breach.
Customer's Data concept
Customer data is information a company holds about the people or organizations that use its services.
customer-facing services concept
Customer-facing services are websites, apps, or systems that customers can directly use.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS 3.1 concept
CVSS 3.1 is version 3.1 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System used to rate the severity of security flaws.
CVSS 4.0 concept
CVSS 4.0 is a standard scoring system used to rate how serious a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS
CVSS 9.3 concept
CVSS 9.3 is a very high vulnerability severity score on a 0-to-10 scale used to show how serious a security flaw is.
CVSS 9.8 concept
A very high severity score on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System scale.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS score: 9.8
CVSS score of 9.8 concept
A very high rating on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, indicating a critical security flaw.
CVSS Scores concept
Standard numerical ratings used to describe the technical severity of software vulnerabilities.
CVSS v4 concept
CVSS v4 is version 4 of a standard scoring system used to describe how severe a security vulnerability is.
CWE-362 vulnerability
A Common Weakness Enumeration identifier for race conditions, where timing between concurrent operations causes unsafe behavior.
CWE-502 vulnerability
CWE-502 is the Common Weakness Enumeration entry for unsafe deserialization, where software processes structured data in a dangerous way.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber incident concept
A cyber incident is any event where digital systems, accounts, or data may have been attacked, exposed, or disrupted.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
cyber operations concept
Activities conducted in cyberspace including espionage, sabotage, or defense, typically by state-sponsored groups.
Cyber risks concept
Cyber risks are the chances that digital systems, data, or services could be harmed by accidents, failures, or attacks.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
cyberattacks concept
Malicious activities conducted over computer networks to steal data, disrupt operations, or damage systems.
also: attacks
cybercrime concept
Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers, networks, or the internet.
cybercrime as a service concept
Cybercrime as a service is when criminals sell ready-made hacking tools, access, or services to other criminals.
cyberespionage technique
The use of computer networks to conduct espionage, usually by state-sponsored groups to steal secrets from governments or corporations.
Cyberespionage Campaign concept
A cyberespionage campaign is a coordinated effort to steal sensitive information from targeted people or organizations using digital means.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
cybersecurity companies organization
Cybersecurity companies are businesses that sell services or products to help protect computers, networks, and data.
cybersecurity experts organization
Cybersecurity experts are people who specialize in protecting computers, networks, and data from attacks.
cybersecurity firms concept
Companies that provide services and products to protect organizations from digital threats.
cybersecurity threats concept
Cybersecurity threats are people, actions, or conditions that could harm computers, networks, accounts, or data.
CyberStrikeAI tool
An open-source framework referenced in security reporting that uses a language model to help direct actions on compromised systems.
Cyble organization
Cyble is a cybersecurity company that provides threat intelligence and digital risk monitoring.
CyCognito organization
CyCognito is a cybersecurity company known for external attack surface management technology.
Da-Yeh University organization
Da-Yeh University is a university in Taiwan.
Daily Cyber Headlines product
A recurring news resource that summarizes cybersecurity headlines.
dashboard tool
A dashboard is a visual interface where users manage settings and view information in a product.
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
Data collection concept
Data collection is the process of gathering information from people, systems, devices, or services for analysis or use.
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
data extortion campaign concept
A data extortion campaign is a series of attacks where criminals steal information and threaten to leak it unless paid.
data loss concept
The accidental or unauthorized destruction, exposure, theft, or unavailability of data.
Data Overwrite technique
An error or attack that replaces existing data with new data, potentially damaging information or program memory.
Data Plane concept
The data plane is the part of a system that handles actual user data, as opposed to the management functions that configure the system.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
Datadog Security Labs organization
Datadog Security Labs is Datadog’s security research team that publishes threat and vulnerability research.
datasets concept
Datasets are collections of information that researchers or tools analyze to find patterns and evidence.
Debian product
A well-known community-driven Linux distribution famous for its stability and package management system.
Debian Security Tracker organization
A Debian project website that tracks known security issues and fixes for Debian software packages.
Debug technique
Debug means to inspect software or systems to find and fix errors, and attackers can sometimes abuse debugging features to learn how something works.
Decentralized exchange product
A cryptocurrency trading service that lets users swap tokens directly without a traditional central exchange operator.
Decentralized Exchange Liquidity Pools concept
Pools of cryptocurrency funds used by decentralized exchanges to make token trading possible without a traditional intermediary.
deception technique
Deception is tricking a person or system into believing something false, often to gain access or hide activity.
Decrypt technique
Decrypt is a cryptographic operation that turns encrypted data back into readable data when the correct key is used.
Deepfake Video concept
A deepfake video is a video altered or generated with AI to make a person appear to say or do something they did not.
deepfakes concept
Realistic but fake images, videos, or audio created using artificial intelligence to show someone saying or doing something they never did.
also: deepfake videos
DeepSeek organization
DeepSeek is an AI service provider referenced in the article.
DeepSeek Models product
Artificial-intelligence language models made by DeepSeek that can generate and analyze text or code.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash product
An AI language-model product referenced in security reporting.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro product
An AI language-model product referenced in security reporting.
default credentials concept
Default credentials are factory-set usernames and passwords that should be changed because attackers often know them.
default search engine product
A default search engine is the search service a browser uses automatically when you type a query into the address bar.
default search provider concept
A default search provider is the search engine a browser uses automatically when someone searches from the address bar.
Defend concept
Defend means to protect systems, networks, data, or users from cyber threats.
Defender product
Defender usually refers to Microsoft Defender, Microsoft’s built-in security and antimalware product line.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
Defense Ministry organization
A Defense Ministry is a government department responsible for national defense, military administration, and related policy.
Delegated Session concept
A login session in which one person or service acts using permissions granted by another user or system.
also: delegated sessions
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
delivery channel concept
The method or medium used to distribute malware or phishing, such as email, SMS, or malicious ads.
demo concept
A demo environment is a system set up to demonstrate software or features, rather than serve real users.
denial-of-service
Denial-of-service is an attack that overwhelms a system so legitimate users cannot access it.
denial-of-service conditions concept
A state in which a service becomes unavailable or unreliable because it is overloaded or disrupted.
denmark other
Denmark is a country in Northern Europe.
Department of Transportation organization
The Department of Transportation is a government agency responsible for transportation systems, rules, and safety.
dependencies concept
Dependencies are outside software components that a project relies on to work.
dependency concept
A dependency is outside software that an application relies on, which can create risk if that outside component is vulnerable or malicious.
Deployments concept
The process of releasing software, configuration changes, or services into a live environment.
deserialization flaw vulnerability
A deserialization flaw is a software bug where unsafe data is loaded back into a program in a way attackers can abuse.
deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability
Deserialization of untrusted data is a dangerous software flaw where an app reads attacker-controlled data as objects, potentially letting the attacker run code or change behavior.
destroy_v6 malware
destroy_v6 is a file-deleting malware tool used to erase data on VMware ESXi systems.
also: Linux ELF wiper
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detection rules concept
Detection rules are instructions security tools use to flag suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.
Detection Signals concept
Alerts or indicators sent by a system when it finds something suspicious.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
Developer Tools product
Developer Tools are software features and applications that help programmers create, test, and troubleshoot software.
developer's machine concept
A developer's machine is a computer used by a software developer to write, build, or test code.
device performance concept
Device performance is how reliably and effectively a device carries out its intended job.
digital services concept
Digital services are online or computer-based services such as websites, apps, portals, and cloud systems.
digital wallets product
Digital wallets are apps or services that store payment information, cryptocurrency keys, or other digital assets.
direct dependencies concept
Direct dependencies are software packages that a project explicitly includes and relies on.
Dirty Frag vulnerability
A vulnerability or exploit technique involving fragmented memory or network packets, similar to Dirty Pipe/Frag attacks.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
discord product
Discord is a communication platform for text, voice, and video chats, popular with gaming and online communities.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
Disposable infrastructure concept
Disposable infrastructure is temporary attacker-controlled servers, domains, or accounts that can be quickly abandoned and replaced.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
disruptive concept
Disruptive describes activity that interrupts normal use of a system, service, or business process.
distinct() technique
A data-processing operation that removes duplicate entries from a dataset.
Distribution Policies concept
Rules that control how products, services, or access are provided through sales and delivery channels.
DIVD organization
DIVD, the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, is a Dutch nonprofit organization that helps identify and report security flaws.
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
DKIM signing domain protocol
The DKIM signing domain is the domain name that cryptographically signs an email to help prove the message was authorized by that domain.
DMARC protocol
DMARC is an email policy check that uses SPF or DKIM alignment to help determine whether a message claiming to come from a domain should be trusted.
DNS protocol
DNS is the internet system that turns human-readable names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use to find websites and services.
also: actively resolving DNS, DNS resolution, DNS and web filtering, DNS logs
DNS Loophole technique
A weakness involving DNS that can bypass intended network restrictions or allow unintended internet access.
DNS-over-HTTPS protocol
DNS-over-HTTPS is a protocol that encrypts DNS lookups by sending them through HTTPS, making browsing requests harder to monitor or tamper with.
docker
Docker is a platform for packaging and running applications in containers.
docs: dependency audit notes other
A pull-request title used to label a proposed change to a software repository.
Domain registration concept
Domain registration is the process of reserving an internet name, such as example.com, so it can be used for a website or email.
Domain Registration Records concept
Information about a domain name's registration, such as its registrar, creation date, and listed contact details.
also: registration data, Registration record
domains concept
Domains are human-readable internet names used to identify online locations.
Downdetector product
Downdetector is a website that tracks user reports of outages for online services and apps.
downtime concept
Downtime is a period when a system, website, or service is unavailable or not working.
dragonforce
DragonForce is a ransomware group that extorts victims by stealing data and encrypting systems.
also: DragonForce Actors
DREAM_ANNEXATION.txt malware
DREAM_ANNEXATION.txt is a text-file name associated with the destroy_v6 wiper.
Drift product
Drift is a customer messaging and marketing platform used by businesses to chat with website visitors and manage sales conversations.
Dutch National High Tech Crime Unit organization
The Dutch National High Tech Crime Unit is a Dutch police unit focused on high-tech crime.
DynamicCLI product
DynamicCLI is a Check Point management interface referenced in security reporting.
DynamicCLI interface product
The DynamicCLI interface is a Check Point management interface that can be affected by security flaws.
also: DynamicCLI IPC interface
edge rendering technique
Edge rendering is web rendering performed on servers close to users at the edge of a network.
also: edge-runtime
EDI protocol
EDI, or electronic data interchange, is a standard way for businesses to exchange documents such as orders and invoices electronically.
EDR product
EDR is security software that monitors computers and servers for suspicious activity and helps respond to attacks.
egress concept
Egress is outbound traffic or data leaving a network, system, or cloud environment.
egress-filtering concept
The practice of monitoring and controlling data leaving a network to prevent data exfiltration.
ELEVATE technique
ELEVATE is a named privilege-raising or exploitation step referenced in security reporting.
Elevate privileges technique
To gain higher-level permissions on a system than a user or attacker originally had.
Elevated concept
Elevated means running with higher permissions than a normal user, such as administrator-level access.
elevated permissions concept
Higher-level access rights that let a user or program make important changes to a computer or network.
ElevenLabs organization
ElevenLabs is an AI company known for services that generate realistic synthetic speech and voices.
email accounts concept
Email accounts are user accounts that let people send, receive, and store email messages.
email addresses concept
Email addresses are the unique names people use to send and receive email, such as user@example.com.
email authentication concept
Technical methods that verify an email came from the domain it claims and hasn't been forged.
email authentication checks technique
Email authentication checks are tests such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC that help verify whether an email really came from the domain it claims.
Email Data concept
Email data includes message contents, attachments, sender and recipient details, and mailbox information.
Email Distribution Service concept
A service used to send large numbers of emails, such as newsletters or announcements.
also: email distribution provider, email infrastructure, email distribution records
Email security concept
Email security protects inboxes and users from threats such as phishing, malware, and scam messages.
Email system product
An email system is the software and services used to send, receive, store, and filter email.
email traffic concept
Messages and related data moving between email systems and users.
Emerging Tech: Security — Cloud Investigation and Response Automation Offers Transformation Opportunities other
A Gartner report about technologies and practices for investigating and responding to cloud security incidents.
employee’s credentials concept
An employee's login information, such as a username, password, security key, or authentication token.
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
Encrypted connections protocol
Network connections that scramble data so outsiders cannot easily read it while it is being sent.
Encryption keys concept
Encryption keys are secret values used to lock and unlock protected data.
end of life concept
The point when a vendor stops supporting a product, including no longer providing security fixes.
end-of-life versions concept
Older software versions that are no longer officially supported or routinely updated by their maker.
End-users concept
End-users are the people who actually use a system, app, or service.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
Endpoint Analysis technique
The examination of activity on a computer or other device to determine what happened and how to respond.
endpoint management concept
Endpoint management is the practice of monitoring, configuring, and securing devices such as laptops, desktops, and phones.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
also: devices
enforcement mode concept
A security setting mode that actively applies a policy rather than only monitoring or reporting violations.
entra-id
Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft’s cloud identity service, formerly called Azure Active Directory.
also: Azure AD
entry point concept
An entry point is the place or method an attacker, program, or process first uses to get into a system or workflow.
entry points concept
Entry points are the places where attackers can first get into a system or network.
environment variables concept
Environment variables are named settings stored by an operating system or runtime that programs can read while they run.
erasing traces of activity technique
Erasing traces of activity means removing logs, files, or other evidence to hide an attacker's actions.
also: removing evidence
Error Messages concept
Error messages are notices from software explaining that something failed or did not work as expected.
Escalate privileges technique
To escalate privileges means to gain higher-level access on a system than you were originally allowed to have.
also: escalate privileges to root
escalation paths concept
Escalation paths are agreed steps for passing an issue to the people or teams able to handle it.
Escape organization
Escape is a company that provides security testing tools for application programming interfaces.
escaping technique
Escaping means changing special characters in text so a computer treats them as normal text instead of as commands or code.
eset
ESET is a cybersecurity company that makes antivirus, endpoint protection, and threat research products.
espionage concept
Espionage is spying to gather information without permission.
Espionage Activity concept
Espionage activity is the secret collection of information for political, military, economic, or strategic advantage.
espionage groups threat-actor
Espionage groups are attackers who secretly steal information for spying, often on behalf of a government or organization.
Espionage operations concept
Espionage operations are spying activities carried out to steal sensitive information, often for a government or organization.
ESXi product
ESXi is VMware's bare-metal hypervisor used to run virtual machines on servers.
ESXi implant malware
An ESXi implant is malicious software installed on a VMware ESXi virtualization host to give an attacker access or control.
Eurojust organization
Eurojust is the European Union agency that helps countries cooperate on criminal justice investigations.
europe
Europe is a continent often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regulations, victims, threat activity, or law enforcement.
European authorities organization
European authorities refers to government or law-enforcement agencies in Europe involved in investigations or enforcement actions.
European Commission organization
European Commission is the European Union's executive body that proposes laws, enforces rules, and oversees policy.
European intelligence services organization
European intelligence services are government agencies in Europe that collect and analyze security information.
european-union
The European Union is a political and economic union of European countries that also creates cybersecurity and privacy rules.
Europol organization
Europol is the European Union’s law enforcement agency that helps member countries fight serious and organized crime.
evasion technique
A technique used by attackers to avoid detection by security tools like antivirus or firewalls.
evil-corp threat-actor
Evil Corp is a Russian cybercrime group associated with banking malware and ransomware operations.
Exchange Online product
Exchange Online is Microsoft’s cloud-hosted email and calendar service in Microsoft 365.
Exchange Online EWS Apps product
Applications that use Exchange Web Services to access mailboxes in Microsoft's Exchange Online email service.
executable concept
An executable is a file that can run as a program on a computer.
also: precompiled executable
executable code concept
Instructions that a computer can run to perform actions.
Executable Payload malware
A program file delivered by an attacker that can run code on a victim's computer.
Execute code concept
Execute code means to make a computer run instructions, which is dangerous if an attacker can run their own code.
Execute Commands technique
Executing commands means instructing a computer to perform actions through its command line or operating system.
Execution technique
Execution is the stage where an attacker runs code or commands on a target system.
exfiltrate technique
To exfiltrate means to secretly move stolen data out of a system or network.
exfiltration technique
Exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or theft of data from a system or organization.
Experimental concept
Experimental is a label for a feature or tool that is still being tested and may change or be unsafe for production use.
exploit technique
An exploit is code or a method that takes advantage of a security flaw to make something happen that should not be allowed.
exploit chain technique
A sequence of multiple security exploits used one after another to break into a system step by step.
exploit payload technique
An exploit payload is the data or code sent to trigger a vulnerability and produce a desired effect.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.
exploitation attempts technique
Exploitation attempts are tries to take advantage of a software weakness to gain access, run code, or cause harm.
Exploitation in the wild concept
Exploitation in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just testing it in a lab.
Exploitation: none concept
Exploitation: none means there is no known evidence that a vulnerability has been actively used in attacks.
Exploited technique
Exploited means attackers successfully took advantage of a weakness in software or a system.
Exploited flaws concept
Exploited flaws are security weaknesses that attackers have actively used to gain access, disrupt systems, or steal information.
Exploits technique
Exploits are code or techniques that take advantage of software vulnerabilities.
Explosives concept
Materials that can rapidly release energy and cause an explosion.
Exposed concept
Accessible in a way that could allow a threat to reach or affect a system.
exposed credentials concept
Login details that have been accidentally published or stolen, granting unauthorized access.
exposed secrets concept
Exposed secrets are leaked passwords, API keys, tokens, or other sensitive credentials that attackers could use.
exposed server concept
An exposed server is a server reachable from the internet or another network where unauthorized people may find it.
also: The server
Exposed Systems concept
Exposed systems are computers or services reachable by outsiders, often through the public internet.
external attack surface concept
An external attack surface is everything an organization exposes to the internet that attackers could try to target.
external databases concept
External databases are databases located on separate systems that another application or database connects to.
External layer concept
The external layer is the public-facing part of a cloud environment, including internet-accessible consoles, APIs, and service endpoints.
also: External
External Network concept
The internet-facing parts of an organization's network that can be reached from outside the organization.
External services concept
External services are third-party systems or online services that an application depends on but does not directly control.
Extortion Attacks technique
Extortion attacks are cyberattacks where criminals pressure victims to pay money, often by threatening to leak stolen data or keep systems disrupted.
FaceStealer malware
A threat campaign or malware operation associated with stealing information through deceptive social-engineering tactics.
also: North Korea’s FaceStealer
fake Cloudflare verification page technique
A fake Cloudflare verification page is a deceptive web page that imitates a security check to persuade visitors to perform unsafe actions.
Fake login pages technique
Fake login pages are imitation sign-in screens used to trick people into entering their usernames, passwords, or one-time codes.
fake websites concept
Fake websites are lookalike or fraudulent sites made to trick visitors into giving up money, passwords, or information.
Falcon threat-actor
An extortion-related threat-actor name referenced in security reporting.
Falcon C2 tool
Falcon C2 is a command-and-control framework that attackers can use to communicate with and control compromised browsers or devices.
fbi organization
The FBI is the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, which investigates cybercrime and national security threats.
FDA organization
The FDA, or U.S. Food and Drug Administration, is the government agency that regulates food, medicines, and medical devices.
Federal Aviation Administration organization
The U.S. government agency that regulates civil aviation and air-travel safety.
Federal Bureau of Investigation organization
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is the main U.S. federal law-enforcement agency that investigates crimes including cybercrime.
federal regulators organization
Federal regulators are government agencies that enforce rules and laws for industries or public services at the national level.
federated identity credentials concept
Credentials that let an application trust identity tokens from an external system instead of storing a secret.
fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors product
Fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors are server CPUs made by AMD under the Turin codename.
also: earlier EPYC processors, AMD EPYC Turin CPU
file creation technique
File creation is the act of making a new file on a computer or server, which can matter in security if attackers create files to gain control or hide activity.
File system concept
A file system is the way an operating system organizes and stores files on a disk or device.
File-Transfer Vulnerability vulnerability
A security weakness in a file-transfer feature that could let an attacker send or receive harmful files.
also: file-transfer
Filtering technique
The process of narrowing data, such as logs, to show only entries matching selected details.
financial institutions organization
Financial institutions are organizations such as banks, credit unions, insurers, and investment firms that handle money and financial services.
financial services organization
Financial services are businesses such as banks, payment companies, insurers, and investment firms that manage money or financial transactions.
fingerprinting technique
Fingerprinting is collecting clues about a device, user, or system to identify it or tailor an attack.
fingerprints concept
Fingerprints are unique identifying clues, such as file hashes or device traits, that help recognize a person, system, or file.
firewall product
A firewall is a security system that controls what network traffic is allowed in or out.
Firewall rules concept
Firewall rules are settings that decide which network traffic is allowed or blocked.
firmware concept
Firmware is the built-in software that controls hardware devices such as routers, phones, or embedded systems.
flaw concept
A flaw is a weakness or mistake in software, design, or configuration that can cause problems or security risk.
FlexPLM product
FlexPLM is a PTC product used by companies to manage product lifecycle information, especially in retail, fashion, and manufacturing contexts.
Flight Check-In concept
The process of confirming a passenger's flight and obtaining boarding documents before travel.
also: check-in

A Flight client is the part of a React application that receives and processes React Flight data.
also: client parser, Flight parser
Fly.io GitHub App product
Fly.io GitHub App is an application that users can connect to GitHub to authorize Fly.io to interact with repositories or accounts.
folders concept
Folders are containers used to organize files in a computer system.
force-push technique
A Git command that overwrites remote repository history, sometimes used by attackers to remove traces or disrupt code after gaining access.
Forensic data concept
Forensic data is evidence collected from systems to understand what happened during a security incident.
Forensics concept
Digital forensics is the process of collecting and examining digital evidence after a security incident.
Forks concept
Copies of a software repository that can be changed independently from the original.
Fortune 100 organization
A ranking of the 100 largest U.S. companies by annual revenue published by Fortune magazine.
framing corruption technique
Framing corruption happens when the boundaries between data messages are handled incorrectly, causing data to be interpreted wrongly.
also: framing bug, corrupted stream, corrupted RSC response
france other
France is a country in Western Europe.
French Government organization
The national government of France and its public institutions.

also: From, sender field, visible sender
Fuel the SOC with Identity Context: Securing Humans, Machines, and AI Agents other
A webinar title about adding identity information to security operations.
fulfillment processes concept
Fulfillment processes are the steps used to prepare, deliver, or complete customer orders and services.
full administrative control concept
Full administrative control means having the highest level of access, allowing someone to change settings, install software, and control the system.
full compromise concept
Full compromise means an attacker has gained broad or complete control over an account, system, or environment.
Fullerton Health organization
Fullerton Health is a healthcare organization referenced in security reporting.
fully patched concept
Describes a device or program that has installed all currently available security updates.
G4 product
G4 is a Google Cloud virtual-machine series using AMD-based hardware.
Gap organization
Gap is a clothing and retail company.
gartner organization
Gartner is a research and advisory company that publishes reports about technology and cybersecurity markets.
gateway product
A gateway is a system that sits between networks or services and controls or forwards traffic.
gateways product
Gateways are devices or services that connect one network or system to another and control how traffic passes between them.
gcp product
GCP, or Google Cloud Platform, is Google's cloud computing service for running applications, storing data, and managing infrastructure online.
Gemini product
Gemini is Google’s family of AI models and chatbot products.
generative AI concept
Generative AI is artificial intelligence that can create new text, images, audio, code, or other content from prompts.
German authorities organization
German authorities are government or law-enforcement bodies in Germany.
German Federal Criminal Police Office organization
Germany's national criminal police agency, commonly known as the Bundeskriminalamt or BKA.
